mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, Exalted is He (ويل لكل همزة): (ويل) is nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject), and that is the preferred choice. Its being accusative is permissible, as a maṣdar (verbal noun) or by way of incitement (ighrāʾ). Its explanation has already passed.

mekki-muskil:2-2.t:
His saying (الذي جمع مالا): (الذي) is in the position of the nominative on the implication of a mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. «هو الذي»; or in the position of the accusative on [the implication of] «أعني» (I mean); or in the position of the genitive (khafḍ) as a badal (substitute) for (كل).
His saying (وعدده): (عدد) is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa. Al-Ḥasan read it without doubling, so it is accusative, conjoined to (مال), i.e. «وجمع عدده» (and gathered its number). It is not good for it to be, in the meaning of the doubled form, a past verb with the doubling resolved [i.e. «عَدَدَه»], because resolving the doubling in something like this is not permissible except in poetry.

mekki-muskil:3-3.t:
His saying (يحسب أن ماله أخلده): (أنّ) stands in for the two objects of (حسب).
The kasra and fatḥa of the sīn in (يحسب) are two well-known dialects. It is related that the kasra is the dialect of the Prophet ﷺ, and it is permissible in every imperfect verb from (حسب).

mekki-muskil:4-4.t: His saying (لينبذن): this verb and its like are indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because of the nūn adjoining it, and it contains a pronoun referring to (الذي). Al-Ḥasan read «لينبذانّ» in the dual, referring it back to the wealth and its owner; and it is related from him [that he read] «لينبذُنّ» with ḍamma on the dhāl, in the plural, referring it back to the backbiter (al-humaza), the slanderer (al-lumaza) and the wealth.

mekki-muskil:5-5.t: His saying (وما أدراك ما الحطمة): its mention has already preceded.

mekki-muskil:6-6.t: His saying (نار الله): nominative (marfūʿ) on the implication of «هي»; a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).

mekki-muskil:8-8.t: His saying (مؤصدة): whoever gave it a hamza took it from «آصدت الباب» when you have closed the door, a known dialect. Whoever did not give it a hamza made it a lightened form of the hamza; and it is possible that he took it from «أوصدت», a well-known dialect in it. It is like their saying «وكّدت» and «أكّدت», and «التأكيد» and «التوكيد», with one meaning; and likewise «أرّخت الكتاب» and «ورّخته» (I dated the letter), two dialects. His saying (بالوصيد) indicates «أوصدت» with wāw; had it been from «آصدت», it would have been «بالأصيد».

mekki-muskil:9-9.t: His saying (في عمد): whoever read it with two fatḥas made it a collective noun (ism li-l-jamʿ), because the pattern of «فعول», «فعيل» and «فعال» is to be pluralised on «فُعُل», such as «كتاب» and «كتب», «رسول» and «رسل», «رغيف» and «رغف». They also said «أديم» and «أدم», «أفيق» and «أفق»; so this is on a par with «عمود» and «عمد» with fatḥa.
